subject: Post-call: EU deployment, ops evidence requested + demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@medisant.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: EU deployment constraints, evidence requested, next steps

Claire — thanks for the 45m call this morning. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can kick off next-week items. I’ve bolded owners and deadlines.

Key pain & goals (from Medisant):
- Data residency: all PHI and derived patient tokens must persist and be processed within the EU (Ireland region preferred).
- Air-gap / restricted egress: initial environment will not have general outbound internet. Only specific flows allowed via a controlled proxy/VPN.
- Audit evidence: procurement + security asked for SOC 2 summary, DPA draft, and confirmation on KMS/HSM approach.
- Network constraints: no open outbound 443 to arbitrary hosts; they require IP allowlist + mutual TLS to vendor endpoints.
- Pilot scope: 2 dev/test lanes, one integration sandbox (staging), pilot in production for 1 clinical workflow (Q3 pilot target).

Immediate asks we committed to during the call:
1) Send SOC 2 summary + DPA template (Marissa) — by EOD Thu 19 Feb.
2) Provide networking constraints checklist and recommended connectivity patterns (Ben) — draft by Mon 23 Feb.
3) Technical deep-dive / demo for network team + infra on allowed deployment modes (Laura to schedule) — target week of 2 Mar.
4) Confirm HSM/KMS integration options and whether customer-managed keys are supported in Private deployments (Marissa) — short note in the materials.

Notes on feasibility / quick engineering takeaways:
- Private (VPC) deployment: fully supported; we can follow a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane.
- Air-gap scenarios: we can operate in a restricted egress environment but need an outbound relay for model downloads/patching or a pre-staged image workflow. We described the "airgap image bundle" pattern; we should document the cadence for image refreshes.
- TLS & mTLS: runtime supports client certificate validation for routing to third-party tools and can accept IP allowlists at the load balancer + firewall.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (stub), redwood-dpa-template.docx (stub), networking-checklist.xlsx (stub).

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- I’ll send the evidence + DPA EOD Thu (Marissa).
- Ben will share the networking checklist + recommended patterns by Mon 23 Feb — includes VPN/DirectConnect options and sample iptables/NGINX allowlist rules.
- Laura will propose 2 time slots for a 60m technical demo (target week of Mar 2).

If any of the bullets above are off, flag them and I’ll correct. Appreciate the context — we’ll compile a concise package for Procurement and your security team.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Claire Nguyen <claire@medisant.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Medisant Procurement <procurement@medisant.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: EU deployment constraints, evidence requested, next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear write-up. This aligns with what our InfoSec asked for in the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- For the air-gap: our security team will not allow periodic outbound connections for model updates unless we can attest and schedule them under change control. A pre-staged image path is preferred.
- KMS: we need a confirmation that HSM-backed keys (Azure Key Vault or AWS CloudHSM) can be used and that key material never leaves the HSM.
- Network connectivity: we have an existing site-to-site VPN to Azure; if you can provide a Direct Connect / ExpressRoute alternative that may be cleaner for throughput.

Procurement will review the DPA; please cc the procurement mailbox on the DPA. For the demo, we’d like the VPN/networking portion to be first; our network lead (Tom Barrett) will join. Tom's email: tom.barrett@medisant.com.

Thanks — Claire
Director, Platform Security
Medisant Clinic

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: EU deployment constraints, evidence requested, next steps

Claire — quick networking checklist draft attached. Highlights:

- Recommended connectivity: site-to-site VPN for pilot -> ExpressRoute/DirectConnect for production. We included a short tradeoff table (throughput, SLA, ops overhead).
- IP allowlist: we need a /28 open to our egress relay for the controlled update window. If you prefer mTLS only, we can remove IP allowlist but require cert distribution.
- Image refreshes: propose a quarterly scheduled refresh with an option for emergency security patches (change-control approved).
- Egress proxies: we support proxying update metadata over TLS through a customer-controlled proxy; payloads can be delivered by pre-staged S3-compatible artifacts in your region.

Attached: networking-checklist.xlsx (stub). I’ll update with sample security group snippets and an example iptables rule set if that will help Tom.

—Ben
